author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Switzerland’s Audrey Werro won the women’s 800 meters at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, defeating Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson in one of the meet’s most anticipated races. Werro led from the front and finished in 1 minute, 55.88 seconds.

Hodgkinson placed second in 1:56.26, while Femke Broeders-Bol finished third. The victory completed an unbeaten outdoor season for the 22-year-old Werro, whose rapid rise has made the women’s 800 one of track’s most competitive events. Her season included a European title and a personal best of 1:53.70.

Werro earned $150,000 from the championship’s $10 million prize pool. Beyond the payout, the win gave her the first Ultimate Championship title in the event and another direct victory over an established Olympic champion. The result also reinforced the depth of the current 800-meter rivalry, with several runners producing times that have renewed attention around a world record that has stood since 1983. Budapest closed Werro’s outdoor campaign with a controlled championship performance rather than a late tactical surge.
dek: The 22-year-old Swiss runner led throughout and finished in 1:55.88 ahead of Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson.
headline: Audrey Werro beats Keely Hodgkinson for Ultimate Championship 800-meter title
